candidates.title: Deep learning–based CT segmentation of mandibular bone invasion in oral squamous cell carcinoma
candidates.abstract: Abstract Background Accurate identification of mandibular invasion by oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is important for virtual surgical planning, but manual delineation on CT is challenging and time-consuming. This retrospective proof-of-concept study evaluated automated segmentation of the mandible and radiologically apparent bone invasion and explored centerline-based assessment of longitudinal tumor extent for computer-aided design/computer-aided manufacturing (CAD/CAM) planning. Methods Fifty preoperative CT examinations from 50 patients with histopathologically confirmed mandibular invasion were included. Thirty examinations were used for model development and 20 for independent testing. A three-dimensional MedNeXt architecture implemented within nnU-Net was trained applying expert-reviewed CT reference segmentations. Performance was assessed using Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), precision, recall, average symmetric surface distance and 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance. Spatial localization, longitudinal invasion-span differences and signed centerline-projected endpoint errors were assessed in the holdout cohort. Results Mean mandibular DSC was 0.965 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.961–0.969; median 0.967). Mean invasion DSC was 0.553 (95% CI, 0.425–0.660; median 0.623), with mean precision of 0.742 and recall of 0.483. Predicted invasion overlapped the CT reference in 18/20 examinations (90%); 16/20 (80%) achieved DSC ≥ 0.20. Two cases were completely missed. Among the 18 evaluable cases, the median absolute invasion-span difference was 7.01 mm (interquartile range, 5.08–13.00 mm) and the median symmetric endpoint distance was 5.88 mm (3.19–9.16 mm). Conclusions The present proof-of-concept study demonstrates the technical feasibility of automated CT segmentation of the mandible and radiologically apparent mandibular invasion by OSCC. The approach may support transmission of radiological tumor extent into virtual resection planning. Larger multicenter studies and prospective clinical validation are needed to establish its impact on planning accuracy and workflow efficiency.

candidates.title: High-Strength Deep Learning Image Reconstruction Versus Adaptive Statistical Iterative Reconstruction for Stenosis Assessment in Stented Coronary Vessels on Coronary CT Angiography: A Multireader Study
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: To compare high-strength deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR-H) with adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction (ASIR-V) for coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) of stented vessels, evaluating image quality, stenosis measurement accuracy, and classification performance against invasive coronary angiography (ICA) as reference standard. Methods: This retrospective single-centre study included 20 patients (30 coronary vessels) with prior stent implantation and ≥50% stenosis on CCTA. Datasets were reconstructed using ASIR-V and DLIR-H. Four blinded readers assessed subjective image quality and in-stent lumen and vessel stenosis degree; Bayesian hierarchical models accounted for reader and vessel variability. Results: DLIR-H improved subjective noise ratings (posterior probability >99%) and reduced in-stent lumen stenosis measurement error by approximately 15% (estimate: −0.16; 90% credible interval: −0.30 to −0.01; probability: 96%), with no clear evidence of an effect on native-vessel stenosis measurement error (probability: 72%). False-positive stent-level classifications (CAD-RADS ≥4) decreased from 10 to 4 reader assessments, whereas false-negative classifications increased from 2 to 4. Only one stent was reference-positive on ICA. Inter-reader agreement was similar for both reconstructions. Conclusions: In this exploratory study, DLIR-H was associated with a modest reduction in in-stent lumen stenosis measurement error, with no benefit for native vessel stenosis. At the stent level, DLIR-H shifted classifications towards CAD-RADS ≤3 but did not improve classification accuracy. Inter-reader agreement was limited with both reconstructions. Given the small sample and the single stent with ≥70% stenosis on ICA, these findings should be regarded as preliminary and require confirmation before informing routine clinical use.

candidates.title: AI agents can redesign engineering parts with more than a thousand CAD parameters and nonlinear simulations
candidates.abstract: Simulation-driven design of real engineering components has to meet three conditions at once. It runs on few solves, since a nonlinear finite-element simulation of a 3D part takes hours; its design space has many values, the hundreds to thousands of values of the part's CAD model; and a better design often needs a redesign, coordinated changes of the part's proportions rather than local polishing of its surface. Automated optimisers meet at most two of these conditions. Classical optimisers, Bayesian or derivative-free, need a person to cut the design down to a few parameters, and on all the values they need far more solves; industrial shape optimisers move every surface node of the mesh in one solve per cycle, but only in small steps that polish rather than redesign. We ask whether a general-purpose large language model (LLM) can meet all three by joining what it knows with what the simulation shows. GPT-6 Astra edits a magnesium stent through a CAD geometry parametrisation of about 1,650 values, with a budget of 15 simulations; every proposal is built in CAD, meshed and simulated with large-deformation plasticity and contact, and the LLM reads the full results of every solve. Within that budget it lowered the objective, a high percentile of the strains in the stent's bends, by 32%; on the same budget, the industrial shape optimiser Tosca improved the original design by a tenth and then stopped improving. An earlier GPT-6 Astra design, 25% lower in the same objective, was checked in an independent, higher-fidelity model of the full deployment with crimping and damage: it was 14% less strained than the original after the full chain, and its most damaged spot began to fail later and carried 63% less damage at full expansion. LLMs can thus join their learned knowledge with simulation data to adjust more than a thousand design values and reach valid designs with real improvements.

candidates.title: BRepDSN: A Dual-stream Network Design for B-Rep Representation Learning Leveraging the Duality of Face and Boundary Vertices
candidates.abstract: Designing a neural network for Boundary Representation (B-Rep) models impacts fundamental tasks in Computer-Aided Design (CAD), Engineering (CAE), and Manufacturing (CAM). Existing methods primarily leverage face adjacency for B-Rep feature encoding, overlooking crucial boundary features from the B-Rep vertices. To address this, we introduce a novel dual-stream neural network, called BRepDSN, that explicitly leverages complementary features from both a Face-adjacency Graph (FG) and a Vertex-adjacency Graph (VG). Our method employs alternating message passing between these two graph streams with bidirectional information exchange. Specifically, faces gather boundary-aware cues from incident vertices through a dual mapping, while vertices are refined by face-level context, ensuring boundary-aware and semantically aligned feature encoding. To further boost the performance, we propose a face-vertex contrastive objective. This objective constructs contrastive pairs based on the duality between a face’s embedding and the aggregated embedding of its boundary vertices. Additionally, for segmentation tasks, we use an auxiliary classification loss to determine boundary edges, which acts as a dual task to the main face segmentation. BRepDSN can be used for multiple B-Rep processing tasks. We evaluate the following example tasks: 1) B-Rep Modeling Operation Segmentation, 2) Operation Step Segmentation, 3) B-Rep Classification, 4) Machining Feature Segmentation, and 5) Assembly Mating. Extensive experiments show that our method sets a new state of the art on all five tasks. For example, our method outperforms competing methods on the B-Rep modeling operation segmentation of CC3D (+14.65% mIoU), B-Rep classification of TMCAD (+4.9% oAcc), and the mating task of AutoMate [18] (+23.6% location acc, +21.0% type acc). The code for this paper are available on: https://github.com/shinodashx/BrepDSN.

candidates.title: A Carbon Break-Even Framework for Computational Generative Design: Formulation and a Proof-of-Concept on Real CAD Geometries
candidates.abstract: Computational generative design, including topology optimization and AI-assisted text-to-CAD tools, is promoted as a route to lighter, lower-carbon products, yet the electricity of the design computation itself is rarely counted. This study proposes a carbon break-even framework that adapts the indifference-point concept from computer-hardware sustainability analysis to product redesign, defining a break-even production volume, a net environmental return, and a carbon return on investment within a cradle-to-gate boundary. As a computational proof of concept, a three-dimensional SIMP topology-optimization solver instrumented with CodeCarbon redesigned 20 CAD geometries from the Fusion 360 Gallery under a generic load case, primary aluminum, CNC machining, and an imposed 30% volume reduction. Under these assumptions, all redesigns broke even before one unit was produced (median 0.016 units; maximum 0.39) while retaining, for the analyzed load case, the stiffness of 13 of 14 comparable original parts. Sensitivity analyses show that this outcome is conditional: break-even within one unit no longer holds for every part with recycled aluminum (18 of 20 parts) or for mass reductions below about 12%, the break-even volume grows by over four orders of magnitude with larger meshes or other computational backends, and the saving reverses when the redesign requires laser powder bed fusion.

candidates.title: DrawScore: Evaluating Generated CAD Models against Engineering Drawings
candidates.abstract: Automatic CAD generation is commonly evaluated with volumetric IoU, Chamfer Distance, and surface F-score, which barely penalize local errors that occupy only a small fraction of a part's volume or surface area, such as a misplaced hole or a slot on the wrong face, even though such errors are critical to manufacturing. We formalize these metrics in a unified integral form and show that the weight of a local error decays as the $(k+q)$-th power of its size, where $k$ is the dimension of the integration domain and $q$ is determined by the penalty function. Guided by this analysis, we propose DrawScore, which projects both models into three orthographic views with visible and hidden lines, as in engineering drawings, and applies a saturating penalty along the projected curves, so that the weight of a local error decays only linearly. Controlled experiments confirm the predicted decay orders, and on outputs of existing CAD generation agents, DrawScore exposes errors in outputs that IoU rates as nearly perfect. DrawScore further improves generation as a reinforcement learning reward and, for CAD generation from engineering drawings, serves as a test-time verifier without 3D ground truth or an additional reward model. Our code is available at https://github.com/UESTC-Simon/DrawScore.

candidates.title: Machine-Learning Algorithms and Benchmarking Missing-Data Strategies for Predicting Angiographically Severe Coronary Artery Stenosis: A Retrospective Study
candidates.abstract: Background Missing data is common in clinical datasets used to predict coronary artery disease (CAD) and can influence the relative performance of machine learning algorithms. This study evaluated and compared missing data handling strategies and machine learning models for predicting clinically significant coronary artery stenosis (70% or greater) using clinical variables. Methods In this retrospective single-center study, 623 patients undergoing coronary angiography were analyzed. We evaluated three missing-data strategies: indicator-based imputation, MICE-based iterative imputation, and k-nearest neighbor (KNN) imputation in combination with eight machine-learning algorithms, yielding 24 workflows. Model development used an 80/20 stratified train-test split, nested 5-fold cross-validation, randomized hyperparameter optimization, SMOTENC applied within training folds to handle class imbalance, and probability calibration. We selected the final model based primarily on mean outer cross-validated ROC-AUC, using mean outer Brier score as a tie-breaker. We derived the decision threshold from development-set out-of-fold predictions and applied it unchanged to the held-out test set. Model interpretation included SHAP analysis, permutation importance, and a surrogate decision tree. Results We selected the indicator-based imputation plus linear support vector machine (SVM) workflow, with a mean outer cross-validated ROC-AUC of 0.730 ± 0.069. On the test set, the model achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.759 (95% CI: 0.667–0.843) and a Brier score of 0.182. At the locked threshold of 0.6346, selected from development-set out-of-fold calibrated probabilities by maximizing balanced accuracy, balanced accuracy was 0.726, with a sensitivity of 75.3%, specificity of 70.0%, precision of 84.2%, and negative predictive value of 57.1%. SHAP analysis identified age, LVEF, WBC, WMA, and troponin among the variables with the greatest model-attributed importance. The surrogate decision tree reproduced the final model with 80.8% fidelity. Conclusions In this single-center cohort with substantial and heterogeneous missingness, predictive performance varied across missing-data and modeling strategies, while more complex learners did not demonstrate a discrimination advantage over a regularized linear SVM. The results support the feasibility of a calibrated, missingness-aware machine-learning framework for exploratory CAD risk stratification, but external validation in larger, multicenter populations with different case mix, disease prevalence, and missingness patterns is required before clinical deployment.

candidates.title: MKA: Evaluating Multimodal Knowledge Agents on end-to-end professional tasks
candidates.abstract: We introduce the Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark, which measures how well autonomous agents perform end-to-end professional knowledge work that depends on visual understanding. Each task requires an agent to extract and combine information from multiple visually dense files, such as CAD blueprints, electronics schematics, radiographs, complex charts and geospatial maps, and to produce a standalone deliverable in .xlsx, .pptx, .pdf, .docx, .html or .png format. Existing benchmarks leave this capability largely untested: removing image-viewing tools leaves Gemini 4 Carbon's score on GDPval unchanged, and single-format evaluations such as GDP$.$pdf and GDP$.$xlsx do not require reasoning across files or modalities. MKA contains 200 tasks across 10 economic sectors. Deliverables are graded against expert-weighted rubrics by a sandboxed agentic autorater that agrees with human domain experts on 96.2% of criterion judgments in our expert-graded study (Cohen's $κ= 0.91$), scored by weighted satisfaction rate (WSR) overall and on frontier criteria unsaturated by prior-generation models (Climb-WSR). Across the frontier models we evaluate (Gemini 4 Carbon, Claude Fable 5.2, Claude Opus 5.5, and GPT-6 Astra), Claude Fable 5.2 (56.6% Climb-WSR, 73.3% Overall WSR) and Gemini 4 Carbon (54.3% Climb-WSR, 71.9% Overall WSR) achieve the highest scores, while Carbon uses $5.7\times$ fewer tokens. Even for the strongest models, Climb-WSR remains below 57%, leaving substantial headroom for multimodal agents.

candidates.title: BRepA: Graph-Based B-Rep Pretraining for Unified CAD Understanding and Generation
candidates.abstract: Boundary representation (B-Rep) of CAD models encodes geometric primitives and their relations as a graph structure, enabling efficient shape modeling within CAD software. Learning on B-Reps for downstream tasks, such as segmentation and novel shape generation, requires specialized neural network designs. Moreover, performance improvements and accelerated training can be achieved with effective pretraining strategies, which is particularly important for tasks with limited labeled B-Rep data. In this paper, we introduce BRepA, a unified self-supervised pretraining framework that explicitly reconstructs both the geometry and topology of B-Rep objects via graph-based modeling. By learning from large-scale unlabeled CAD data only once, BRepA produces representations that generalize across tasks and significantly enhance both discriminative and generative learning. On segmentation tasks, BRepA demonstrates remarkable data efficiency. For instance, with only 1% labeled samples, BRepA pretraining improves mIoU by 32.52% compared to models trained from scratch. On generative tasks, aligning diffusion model representations with pretrained BRepA features substantially accelerates convergence, achieving nearly 2 times faster training while improving generation quality under the same computational budget, despite the diffusion model being roughly 20 times larger than BRepA. Overall, our results show that geometry- and topology-aware B-Rep pretraining provides a powerful foundation for both understanding and generating CAD structures, serving as a versatile representation backbone for diverse downstream applications. We will release the code to facilitate future research.

candidates.title: Machine-Learning-Based Forward Modeling of a p-Type Gate-All-Around Junctionless Nanowire Field-Effect Transistor Using Quantum-Corrected Technology Computer-Aided Design
candidates.abstract: Quantum confinement becomes significant once a transistor channel is thinner than about 10 nm, so technology computer-aided design (TCAD) models of such devices must include it. Nearly all machine-learning surrogates reported for gate-all-around junctionless field-effect transistors (GAA-JLFETs) cover n-type devices only, although complementary logic also requires p-type devices. In this work, we calibrated a quantum-corrected drift-diffusion TCAD model against measured data from an n-type GAA-JLFET and then adapted it to a p-type device. Six design parameters were sampled by Latin hypercube sampling, and the transfer characteristic of each design was simulated at drain voltages of −0.1 and −1 V. Runs were retained on the basis of simulation reliability rather than device performance, and the noise floor was set from current samples with a physically impossible sign. The resulting 217 devices were used to train a dilated residual one-dimensional convolutional network that predicts the full transfer curve directly from the design parameters. On 26 held-out test devices, the network reached a median R 2 of 0.9994 and a worst-case R 2 of 0.9959, and it predicted the ON current with a mean error of 1.6%. Each prediction requires a single forward pass instead of a TCAD solve, which removes the simulation bottleneck from the design of p-type GAA-JLFETs.

candidates.title: CADMAGEDDON: High-Fidelity CAD Reconstruction with Local Inference
candidates.abstract: CAD practitioners often work with proprietary parts that they are unwilling to share with external services. For individuals and small companies, bringing this work in-house also requires computational resources they can afford. We introduce CADMAGEDDON, an open-source agent that reconstructs editable CAD from meshes and can run locally on single-GPU systems and current-generation laptops. The method decomposes this complex task into a chain of simple visual decisions about what to construct and what to correct. Geometric tools support precise construction, allowing the agent to focus on visual reasoning. Using the mid-sized Qwen3.8-27B model, CADMAGEDDON outperforms prior approaches, including systems based on frontier models, in reconstruction quality on all the main benchmarks. CADMAGEDDON integrates with FreeCAD, bringing its reconstructions into practitioners' existing CAD workflows. Code: https://github.com/kulibinai/cadmageddon

candidates.title: Assessing the Effects of Design Complexity and Prompt Engineering on CAD Model Generation Using Microsoft Copilot
candidates.abstract: The use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly increasing across various sectors, making tasks more accessible, efficient, and user-friendly. One emerging application is computer-aided design (CAD), where AI has the potential to enable users with little or no-prior CAD experience to create three-dimensional (3D) models through natural-language. Despite growing interest in AI-assisted design, the capability of publicly accessible generative AI systems to reliably generate CAD models across varying levels of design complexity remains insufficiently studied. This work benchmarks the performance of Microsoft Copilot for CAD model generation and investigates the influence of prompt engineering on model quality. A benchmark dataset comprising 60 design tasks was developed and categorized into easy, intermediate, and complex levels. The benchmark included primitive geometries, polygonal and polyhedral models, mechanical components, hollow structures, assemblies, lattice designs, and advanced engineering systems. For each prompt, the generated STL file was evaluated based on geometric accuracy, completeness of requested features, and overall structural validity using commercial software. The results revealed a strong dependence of generation success on design complexity, with easy-level tasks exhibiting high first-attempt success rates, while intermediate and complex tasks frequently required prompt refinement. Prompt length alone was found to have minimal influence on performance; instead, successful CAD generation depended primarily on clearly specified dimensions, geometric features, and functional relationships. Overall, the findings demonstrate that generative AI can lower the barrier to CAD modeling for non-expert users while improving productivity for experienced designers, thereby offering significant potential for engineering design, rapid prototyping, and additive manufacturing applications.

candidates.title: MillBill: A Machining Agent with Geometric Feedback
candidates.abstract: Turning a CAD model into a machining program requires both process knowledge and geometric precision. Language models can generate such workflows by writing geometry and toolpath code for each part, but this makes numerical execution part of the model's task. We introduce MillBill, an agent that separates machining decisions from their geometric execution and verification. Given a boundary-representation part, stock, and material, a locally hosted, mid-sized open model proposes operations and cutting parameters for indexed three-axis machining. A geometric harness generates toolpaths, simulates material removal, and returns feedback for plan refinement. Setup planning accounts for what the available cutters can physically reach, rather than visibility alone. We evaluate the resulting programs by the fraction of the target surface area within the specified tolerance after simulated machining. With Qwen3.8-27B, MillBill outperforms frontier-model approaches that construct their own geometry and toolpath workflows on the evaluated machining tasks. Code: https://github.com/kulibinai/millbill

candidates.title: Generative AI-Driven Parametric Design Optimization Framework for Vehicle Closure Systems
candidates.abstract: This study presents a generative AI-driven parametric design optimization framework integrating performance-oriented generation with editable computer-aided design (CAD) and downstream computer-aided engineering (CAE) analysis for industrial vehicle closure systems. The framework is demonstrated on an automotive tailgate assembly with complex geometry, coupled components, and competing performance and feasibility requirements. A production-oriented CATIA model is restructured into a reference-based parametric template with a 13-dimensional design representation. An automated CAD/CAE workflow generates parametric models, performs structural analysis, and constructs a database of mass, maximum displacement, and maximum von Mises stress. Gaussian process regression surrogates predict performance, while diffusion and flow matching models generate design candidates. The design problem minimizes mass and maximum displacement, with stress assessed as an engineering feasibility constraint. Performance-guided generation using surrogate guidance and performance-aware training using a performance-aware loss incorporate engineering objectives, with sensitivity to guidance scale and loss weight evaluated. Generative search is compared with NSGA-II under matched evaluation budgets using a common surrogate model. Selected Pareto-region candidates are reconstructed in CATIA and re-evaluated through native CAE; all verified candidates are successfully regenerated and analyzed. Relative to the baseline, the knee-point design reduces mass by 7.1% and maximum displacement by 29.4%, while extreme verified solutions achieve maximum reductions of 10.3% and 37.3%, respectively. The results demonstrate performance-oriented multi-objective design exploration compatible with editable industrial CAD and native engineering verification.

candidates.title: INTELLECTUALIZATION OF DESIGN ACTIVITY
candidates.abstract: The article examines the theoretical-methodological and organizational-economic foundations for the intellectualization of design activity within the context of the digital transformation of machine-building enterprises. It substantiates the necessity of transitioning from a traditional model of organizing design work – based primarily on individual professional experience and the use of computer-aided design (CAD) systems – to an ecosystem-based model. This model entails the integration of the intellectual potential of personnel, artificial intelligence technologies, digital engineering tools, corporate knowledge, and organizational-economic mechanisms.The study defines the intellectualization of design activity as a systemic process involving the accumulation, formalization, integration, and practical application of human and artificial intellectual resources, aimed at enhancing the soundness, quality, and effectiveness of design solutions. The paper proposes an original concept for the ecosystem-based organization of a design engineer's work. This model is founded on the functional interaction between the design engineer, the head of the design department, various support functions (technological, production, economic, and information-analytical), external partners, and digital intelligent systems. The key functional components of "intellectualization" are identified: intellectual-analytical, information-knowledge, digital-technological, organizational-coordination, and economic. It is argued that the effectiveness of intellectualization should be evaluated not merely by the level of automation or the reduction in design duration, but also by the quality of design solutions, the minimization of errors and rework, the efficient utilization of intellectual potential, and the overall economic impact on the enterprise. The practical significance of these findings lies in the potential application of the proposed concepts when developing organizational and economic mechanisms to enhance design activities within machine-building enterprises.

candidates.title: Bookkeeping Is Not Judgement: EJBench, an Engineering Judgement Benchmark Built from a Conjugate Heat Transfer Design Campaign
candidates.abstract: We introduce EJBench, a benchmark of engineering judgement: whether a model can predict how a design behaves at new conditions from a few earlier results, and decide on it. Unlike engineering benchmarks that test whether an agent can operate simulation or CAD software, EJBench is software-agnostic and asks what an engineer would conclude without running a simulation. Its tasks come from a conjugate heat transfer design campaign for battery cold plates, in three families: matching unlabelled test results to their operating points, choosing which stored runs to reveal before signing off a design, and ranking new duties by peak cell temperature. Every answer is taken from a converged simulation, not from an LLM judge. The best of ten frontier models, GPT-6 Astra, scores 0.71, and models state almost the same confidence on tasks they get wrong as on tasks they get right. We also post-train Qwen3.5-9B with LoRA and reinforcement learning, rewarded by the share of answer criteria the simulation results confirm; on the held-out test split its score rises from 0.071 to 0.106. We release the train, validation and test splits, the evaluation harness and the leaderboard.

candidates.title: Evaluating generative AI for dimensionally correct and manufacturable CAD models
candidates.abstract: Generative AI now writes Computer-Aided Design (CAD) programs and boundary representations; however, the output that executes or resembles a target need not be dimensionally correct, constrained, or manufacturable. This review asks what evidence supports the engineering validity of generated parametric CAD. Journal articles from 2022 to 2026 were retrieved from OpenAIRE and Crossref, and records outside design geometry were removed. A bibliometric map of 60 articles was combined with manual coding of 19 core studies against a six-rung validation ladder, technical appraisal of ten full texts, and a structured synthesis of 14 matched contrasts. Output rose from three articles in 2022 to 2023 to 50 in 2025 and the partial year 2026, and mentions of feedback loops more than tripled in 2026. Of the coded studies, 14 reported shape fidelity and 10 execution success, but only 3 checked dimensions or explicit constraints, none reported functional analysis, and one measured a manufactured part. Three of six appraised studies with shape metrics normalized scale away. Feedback from interpreters, kernels, or a rule monitor raised execution or validity by 3.9 to 19.4 percentage points, but none was compared with resampling under an equal budget, and shape fidelity fell in four of five contrasts. The highest correction rates, 32.6 to 36.9 points, came from runs two thirds of which carried author-injected defects, certified by the monitor supplying the feedback. No study held out part families. Generative CAD has learned to produce valid programs; evidence that it satisfies engineering requirements remains thin.

candidates.title: Performance prediction of contra-rotating propellers based on Artificial Neural Network and optimisation technique
candidates.abstract: This study presents a machine learning–assisted optimisation framework for the design of contra-rotating propellers (CRPs) to improve hydrodynamic efficiency while accounting for cavitation and noise constraints. A Multiple-Input Multiple-Output Artificial Neural Network (MIMO-ANN) is developed as a surrogate model to predict open-water performance using the thrust loading coefficient (KT/J2), expanded area ratio (EAR) and pitch-to-diameter ratio (P/D) as inputs. The model achieves high predictive accuracy across multiple propeller series, with coefficients of determination (R2) exceeding 0.9996 and root-mean-square errors (RMSE) below 0.005. The ANN is coupled with constrained nonlinear optimisation to maximise open-water efficiency subject to the Keller cavitation criterion and a blade-tip-speed limit. The best-performing CRP configurations achieve efficiencies exceeding 68%, with a maximum of 70.30%, compared with 65.0% for the reference KP505 and 66.71% for the best optimised fixed-pitch propeller (FPP). Including propeller diameter as a decision variable affects thrust loading, rotational speed, and cavitation constraint. Some high-efficiency solutions marginally violate the cavitation constraint because of high operating load and geometric limits of the systematic propeller series; these cases are treated as near-feasible performance boundaries. candidates.title: A Systematic Review on Generative Design for Manufacturability
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being used to support design for manufacturability (DfM) by enabling the generation of manufacturable designs. We refer to this emerging area as generative design for manufacturability (GDfM). Despite growing interest, current literature lacks a dedicated analysis of different approaches for integrating DfM rules in GDfM. This paper presents a systematic review of GDfM based on a PRISMA‐guided search of Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore. Of 1547 identified records, 36 studies were selected for detailed analysis. The reviewed studies are compared by manufacturing process, AI method, and data representation. The results show that the literature is dominated by additive manufacturing, with comparatively fewer studies in machining and very limited coverage of casting, molding, forging, and stamping. DfM rules are integrated into designs via data‐driven approaches and rule‐based filters or optimizers within generative design pipelines. Data‐driven approaches ensure manufacturability via manufacturable datasets, enhanced model training, and modified network architectures. Variational autoencoders (VAEs) and generative adversarial networks (GANs) are the most commonly used AI models, whereas other promising models, such as diffusion models and transformers, remain underexplored. In terms of representation, 2D images and voxels dominate despite limited compatibility with downstream engineering tasks. The review identifies key gaps in GDfM in manufacturing process diversity, datasets, benchmarking, and downstream‐compatible representations, and highlights future opportunities in parametric/CAD sequence–based representations, diffusion and transformer models, and broader coverage of traditional manufacturing processes.

candidates.title: Artificial intelligence for pulmonary tuberculosis detection on chest X-ray images: A systematic review and diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based computer-aided detection (CAD) of tuberculosis (TB) on chest X-ray (CXR) may standardize screening and triage in settings with few radiologists but its accuracy in clinical cohorts remains uncertain. We searched five databases (PubMed, ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore, OpenAlex, Lens.org) on 15 March 2026 for studies published between January 2020 and March 2026, and we appraised these studies using QUADAS-2. Evaluations from clinical cohorts with complete 2 × 2 data and a microbiological or composite reference standard for all participants were pooled using a bivariate random-effects model, with 95% prediction intervals. We accounted for overlapping participants by performing a post hoc analysis with one evaluation per cohort and used GRADE to assess the certainty of the evidence. No protocol was prepared or registered. We included 21 studies (26 evaluations of AI models). Nine evaluations from three independent cohorts were pooled. Pooled sensitivity was 0.896 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.874 to 0.915, prediction interval 0.798 to 0.950) and pooled specificity was 0.689 (95% CI 0.642 to 0.732; prediction interval 0.499 to 0.831). Both confidence intervals include the World Health Organization (WHO) triage thresholds (sensitivity 90%, specificity 70%). When a screening study with partial verification was added, pooled specificity increased to 0.735. Eighteen of 24 assessed evaluations were at high risk of bias and only 1 of 21 studies was prospective, fully verified, externally validated and met the WHO thresholds. Certainty of evidence was low for sensitivity and very low for specificity. A subsequent PubMed search found additional eligible clinical evaluations that were not screened, so the review is incomplete for those studies. In clinical cohorts, AI-CXR sensitivity is close to the WHO triage target, and specificity is close to, but not clearly above, its target. The evidence is pooled across only three cohorts, and specificity varies by product and setting. Thresholds need to be calibrated locally, and prospective, externally validated evaluations are needed before widespread deployment.

candidates.title: Flow-CAD: Flow Matching for Contextual Anomaly Detection and Explanation in Tabular Data
candidates.abstract: Contextual anomaly detection in tabular data aims to identify objects whose behavior is unexpected under their contextual conditions. In data-engineering pipelines, this task screens table rows whose measurements violate context-dependent integrity relationships. Most existing approaches rely on either shallow conditional models with limited distributional expressiveness or localized estimators that require per-context modeling, making it difficult to capture complex conditional relationships and scale to high-dimensional settings. We propose Flow-CAD, a new framework for contextual anomaly detection based on Flow Matching. Flow-CAD learns a single global and amortized conditional generative model that flexibly represents behavioral distributions conditioned on context, without assuming simple parametric forms or retraining local models. To enable robust and interpretable anomaly scoring, we introduce a scale-normalized and truncated residual energy derived from the learned conditional flow, which stabilizes anomaly scores, mitigates domination by extreme deviations, and supports feature-wise attribution. We further provide theoretical insights showing that the proposed residual-based anomaly score is stable under velocity estimation error, and that its Monte Carlo estimator satisfies concentration bounds. Experiments on 20 benchmark datasets with 13 competitors demonstrate that Flow-CAD has the best average rank for PR AUC, ROC AUC, and P@n, highlighting its effectiveness and practicality for contextual anomaly detection in tabular data. We provide the source code at https://github.com/ZhongLIFR/FlowCAD.

candidates.title: Circular Design Frameworks and Tools for Energy-Using Components in the Automotive Industry: A Systematic Literature Review on Usability, Integration, and Sustainability Trade-Offs
candidates.abstract: The transition toward a Circular Economy in the automotive industry demands robust eco-design strategies for complex, energy-using, mechatronic systems. This systematic literature review critically evaluates 30 publications representing 27 distinct frameworks and computational tools for active automotive components. Using a customized Usability Scorecard on a 1–5 quantitative scale, solutions were benchmarked across workflow integration, performance trade-offs, End-of-Life, and Critical Raw Material (CRM) management. Systematic review findings reveal significant methodological gaps: circa 52% of evaluated tools exhibit low CAD/PLM workflow integration relying on manual data entry, while only 30% achieve high integration. For trade-off analysis, most tools, about 80%, rely on static multi-criteria weighting or use offline optimization. Furthermore, CRM tracking is unaddressed in 44% of the tools, rising to circa 60% including purely conceptual methods, with only 22% offering dedicated metrics or Digital Product Passport (DPP) readiness for material traceability. Based on these review findings, future research should investigate and validate automated, open-source AI-driven plug-ins leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) and Digital Twins embedded directly in engineering environments to translate Circular Economy principles and metrics into daily design practices.

candidates.title: Optimization in dentistry using digital resources: a systematic review
candidates.abstract: The development of digital dentistry offers opportunities to enhance the quality of dental treatment for both patients and dentists. Tools such as intraoral scanners, cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), CAD/CAM (Computer-Aided Design/Computer-Aided Manufacturing) systems, 3D printing, virtual planning, and artificial intelligence are being widely employed to refine every stage of dental treatment, from diagnosis to oral rehabilitation. In this context, this study aimed to analyze the key contributions of these technologies to the optimization of dental practice, highlighting their clinical applications, benefits, limitations, and future development prospects. To this end, scientific articles published between 2020 and 2026 and indexed in the PubMed, SciELO, Virtual Health Library (VHL), and Web of Science databases were selected. A total of 115 articles were identified. 35 articles were evaluated in full, with 23 included and analyzed in this systematic review. Clinical studies showed homogeneity in their results, with a Chi-square (X²) value of 71.6% (>50%). Regarding the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool, the overall assessment identified 15 studies with a high risk of bias and 29 studies that failed to meet GRADE criteria. According to the Cochrane tool, the risks of bias did not compromise scientific progress. Analysis of the evidence demonstrated that the use of digital resources provides greater diagnostic precision, reduced chair time, and improved communication between professionals and patients, while also increasing treatment predictability and minimizing errors during laboratory and clinical phases. The integration of artificial intelligence into digital workflows has also expanded capabilities for individualized and automated planning, facilitating more accurate decision-making. Despite these advances, challenges remain regarding high initial investment, the need for continuous professional training, technology upgrade costs, and ethical issues associated with the use of these tools. It is concluded that digital dentistry represents a significant milestone in the evolution of clinical practice, establishing itself as a care model that is increasingly efficient, safe, personalized, and grounded in scientific evidence

candidates.title: Fear of Memorizing Objects: End-to-End Zero-Shot Model-Based Object Detection
candidates.abstract: This paper presents FOMO (Fear of Memorizing Objects), an end-to-end trainable transformer-based architecture for zero-shot model-based object detection. Existing approaches typically follow a proposal-and-match pipeline: target-agnostic mask proposals are generated and then matched to template features in a set of loosely coupled stages, making them susceptible to fragmented proposals in clutter and degraded matching under occlusions. FOMO elegantly replaces this paradigm by injecting object template information early in the detection pipeline: Bidirectional attention between learnable latent tokens, multi-view CAD templates, and query image features produces object-aware image features and conditioned queries which are subsequently decoded into bounding-box and confidence predictions. We train FOMO on Clutter6D, a novel large-scale synthetic dataset with over 500k images featuring more than 10k diverse object models rendered in highly cluttered scenes with multiple instances and varying occlusion levels, which addresses the limited object diversity and lack of realistic dense clutter in existing datasets for training zero-shot multi-instance algorithms. In true zero-shot fashion, FOMO achieves 54.2 mAP on BOP-Classic-Core at 0.23 s per image, ranking second overall with 3.8 pp difference to the top method while being more than 7x faster. Throughout comprehensive ablation studies we investigate and verify architectural design choices.

candidates.title: Predicting Dimensional Errors in FDM Printing Using Neural Networks
candidates.abstract: Dimensional accuracy in additive manufacturing represents a critical factor for the quality of functional parts. This work presents a predictive model based on artificial neural networks to estimate and reduce geometric deviations in polylactic acid parts processed by fused filament fabrication. Using a response surface experimental design, the influence of extruder temperature, bed temperature, printing speed, and layer height on the hole diameter relative to its computer-aided design was evaluated. The geometric discrepancy fed the training of the predictive model, which was subsequently coupled with a genetic algorithm to determine optimal manufacturing parameters. The optimized approach successfully reduced the predicted dimensional error to a minimum of 1.59%, demonstrating its applicability in automated calibration for additive processes.

candidates.title: Digital twin-driven generative design of multi-layer cultivation systems for vertical farming with solar light
candidates.abstract: Multi-layer Cultivation Systems (MCSs) intensify urban food production. Designing MCSs for Vertical Farming with Solar Light (VFSL) delivers energy-saving benefits but is constrained by inter-layer shading, which limits productivity and conflicts with yield requirements. Therefore, optimal conceptual design is crucial. To address how to ensure complex designs meet stakeholder requirements during conceptual design, this study proposes a Digital Twin-driven Generative Design (DTGD) framework. The framework links stakeholder requirements with system architecture, fully incorporating theories related to system architecture, Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE), The Double Diamond (TDD), and Digital twin (DT). Using Digital Twin Modeling (DTM) and Candidate Architecture Decision (CAD) as core methods, it supports the generation and trade-off analysis of multiple Candidate Architectures (CAs). When applied to the design of MCSs in a case study, two CAs (square and zigzag cultivation) are generated. Within a design-stage DT model (an early-stage DT) for light simulation, key A-Frame design variables, including A-Frame Width (FW), A-Frame Height (FH), and the vertical height difference between adjacent planting containers (PCVH), are optimized to identify the optimal design solution. Cultivation experiments using the designed MCSs in a greenhouse in Handan, China, confirmed normal growth of cream lettuce in a single cycle. Based on this empirical data, the estimated annual production potential reaches 49.78 kg·m⁻²·year⁻¹ (assuming ten annual cropping cycles), satisfying the stakeholder yield requirement. This demonstrates the framework's practical feasibility for the evaluated case. Future work may incorporate Large Language Models to enhance automated design generation and explore alternative MCSs for wider urban adoption.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence in Coronary Artery Disease: From Detection to Precision Management
candidates.abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide, yet the landscape is rapidly evolving as artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to its detection, diagnosis, and management. This review surveys the expanding role of AI across the full spectrum of CAD care. In screening, deep-learning electrocardiography and electronic health record-based digital markers enable earlier identification of clinically significant disease. In noninvasive imaging, AI-driven coronary computed tomography angiography automates calcium scoring, derives fractional flow reserve without invasive wires, and quantifies high-risk plaque features that predict incident adverse events. Within the cardiac catheterization laboratory, angiography-derived physiologic assessment and AI-guided intravascular imaging segmentation support real-time procedural decision-making. Beyond diagnosis, machine-learning models integrating multimodality imaging data improve risk stratification over conventional clinical scores, while pharmacogenomic algorithms and wearable-based digital rehabilitation platforms enable patient-centric secondary prevention. Despite this progress, significant challenges persist, including limited evidence from randomized trials, algorithmic bias in underrepresented populations, regulatory uncertainty surrounding software-as-a-medical-device frameworks, and the risk of clinician de-skilling. AI has the potential to act as a collaborative tool that augments-rather than replaces-physician judgment. Future directions include foundation models, multiomics integration, agentic AI workflows, and equity-centered deployment strategies to ensure that AI-driven advances benefit all individuals with CAD.

candidates.title: The Art of Diminishing: Poetic Geometry and Generative Proportion in Tiered Temple of Kathmandu Valley
candidates.abstract: Architecture is often understood through its cultural, historical, and symbolic meanings, yet the physical forms through which these meanings are expressed are governed by systems of geometry, proportion, and order. In the architecture of the Kathmandu Valley, the tiered temple represents a distinctive synthesis of cultural tradition and formal organization. While these temples have been studied through their history, symbolism, religious significance, structural behavior and spatial organization, the geometric relationships that generate and organize their vertical form remain less explicitly understood. The complex appearance of tiered temples suggests an underlying order in the relationship between the plinth, walls, cella, and successive roof tiers. These relationships are not necessarily defined by a single fixed dimension or universally documented rule, but may instead emerge through proportional relationships, recurring geometric conditions, and transformations of form. Understanding these relationships raises the question: can the geometry of tiered temples reveal a systematic logic through which their architectural form was established and transformed? This research investigates the geometry and proportional relationships of selected tiered temples of the Kathmandu Valley through observation, photographic measurement, digital reconstruction, and parametric modeling. By examining the relationship between width, height, tier progression, roof slopes, datum conditions, and the proportions of the temple's major components, the research seeks to identify recurring geometric relationships within the vertical composition of these structures. A Grasshopper-based parametric model is further used to reconstruct and manipulate these relationships, allowing the observed geometric conditions to be explored through controlled transformations of the temple form. Rather than reducing traditional architecture to a fixed mathematical formula, this research approaches geometry as a means of understanding how architectural form may carry, preserve, and transform knowledge across time. The study seeks to re-discover the underlying order within the visual complexity of Kathmandu Valley's tiered temples and to demonstrate how the study of geometry can provide a bridge between cultural tradition, architectural form, and contemporary methods of digital exploration.

candidates.title: GraphCAD: Geometry-Aware Diffusion on Edge-Adjacency Graphs for CAD Generation
candidates.abstract: Generative modeling for Computer-Aided Design (CAD) remains fundamentally challenged by the need to capture the intricate interplay between discrete topological connectivity and precise spatial geometry inherent in Boundary Representations (B-reps). Existing generative approaches largely formulate CAD construction as a sequence modeling problem, but consequently lack an explicit topological inductive bias. In this work, we present GraphCAD, a geometry-aware generative framework that centers modeling on the Edge-Adjacency Graph (EAG), a novel graph-based CAD representation tailored for generative tasks. GraphCAD adopts a hybrid graph diffusion formulation to jointly model the discrete and continuous components of EAG and introduces a geometry-aware denoising mechanism that ''renders'' node attributes into spatial point sets. These point sets are encoded by an SE(3)-equivariant backbone and fused into the node representations, thereby grounding the generative process in physical geometry. To support this study, we construct EAGBench, a large-scale dataset of engineering CAD models. Extensive experiments show that GraphCAD can generate complex CAD models with more than 50 faces and achieves state-of-the-art performance in geometric fidelity and distributional alignment compared with sequence-based baselines.
candidates.venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)

candidates.title: UniFuse-CAD: Multimodal CAD Program Synthesis from Any Combination of Inputs
candidates.abstract: Existing computer-aided design (CAD) reverse engineering methods predominantly rely on a single input modality. Even when certain multimodal models can accommodate multiple inputs, they are typically restricted to selecting only a single modality during inference, failing to fully exploit the complementary potential of diverse information sources. To this end, we propose UniFuse-CAD: a unified multimodal CAD program synthesis framework built upon a Vision-Language Model (VLM), supporting any combination of text, image, and point cloud inputs to generate executable CadQuery programs. Experimental findings reveal significant complementarity among visual modalities, but naively concatenating text with visual features disrupts visual representations and induces negative transfer. To address this issue, we design the Gated Text-to-Visual Injection (GTVI) module, which selectively injects text information into visual tokens via gated cross-attention, combined with a Do-No-Harm training constraint and a text-vision alignment loss, unleashing the performance gains of text on hard samples without harming the visual pathway. Furthermore, to address the limited coverage of advanced design features in existing CAD datasets, we construct ForgeCAD: a large-scale multimodal dataset generated through a Large Language Model (LLM)-driven semantic augmentation pipeline, significantly improving data scale and the diversity of advanced features. Experiments demonstrate that UniFuse-CAD outperforms existing methods across various modality combinations, exhibiting superior reconstruction accuracy and robustness.

candidates.title: PrimitiveCAD: An LLM-Based Point-to-CAD Reconstruction with Primitive-Aware Tokenization and Operation Alignment
candidates.abstract: Large-model-based point-to-CAD generation holds immense potential for advancing industrial design and enhancing 3D modeling efficiency. However, most existing methods approach the problem as a general point-cloud encoding and token prediction task, neglecting the tokenization and supervision specifically for CAD-related primitives. As a result, these methods often struggle to accurately reconstruct the intricate primitive structures. To address this limitation, we propose PrimitiveCAD, a novel multi-stage paradigm for point-to-CAD reconstruction that enhances the geometric accuracy of generated CAD models while better preserving critical geometric features. First, we introduce a primitive-aware point cloud tokenization model, enabling the system to learn more robust geometric representations from CAD point clouds. Next, we perform supervised finetuning on a large language model (LLM) and introduce an operation alignment loss to align key CAD operation frequencies, thereby improving the preservation of global shape features. Finally, we incorporate reinforcement learning (RL) and introduce a feature-line alignment reward to further reduce stochasticity and enhance the fine-grained preservation of geometric features. Experiments on the DeepCAD and Fusion360 datasets show that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in code validity, geometric accuracy, and geometric feature preservation.

candidates.title: A data-efficient PINN-Bayesian optimization framework for state variable active filter design
candidates.abstract: Designing an analog active filter is rarely a single-target exercise: cutoff frequency, quality factor, gain, power draw, total harmonic distortion (THD), and sensitivity to component spread all have to be pulled into line at once. In practice, this still means loop after loop of SPICE runs and manual tweaking, which eats up design time and computing budget alike. This paper instead builds a Bayesian Optimization loop around a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) surrogate to automate the synthesis of State Variable Filters (SVFs). Adaptive sampling of the design space, LTspice-based circuit simulation, PINN surrogate modeling, and Bayesian Optimization are brought together so that optimal component values can be located with far fewer costly simulation runs. By incorporating the governing circuit relationships, analytical transfer function, frequency–response characteristics, and stability constraints into PINN training, the proposed surrogate captures the nonlinear relationship between component values and filter performance while maintaining physical consistency. That trained surrogate then drives the Bayesian search, quickly narrowing in on Pareto-optimal filter configurations across cutoff frequency accuracy, passband gain, quality factor, power consumption, THD, and sensitivity. The resulting design reached a cutoff frequency of 10.01 kHz, a gain of 0.998, a quality factor of 0.709, an estimated active-filter power of 12.4 mW, THD of 0.32%, and a sensitivity index of 0.048, with Bayesian Optimization converging in 37 iterations and an average run time of 42.8 s. Benchmarked against Random Search, Particle Swarm Optimization, Genetic Algorithm, and Differential Evolution, the proposed framework consistently reached lower objective values than any of them. A TL084-based hardware prototype backed up the simulation results as well: measured cutoff frequency, gain, and phase response tracked the LTspice predictions closely, and the absolute THD deviation came in at just 0.04%. Taken together, these results point to a PINN-assisted Bayesian Optimization framework that is efficient, scalable, and well suited to next-generation computer-aided design of analog and mixed-signal circuits.

candidates.title: TempFit: Panoptic Symbol Spotting via Template Fitting
candidates.abstract: In this paper, we introduce TempFit , a novel approach for the problem of Panoptic Symbol Spotting on CAD drawings. Existing methods treat symbol spotting as a per-primitive classification or mask-prediction task, with no explicit constraint enforcing that the primitives assigned to one instance form a spatially connected group. As a result, predictions may erroneously merge primitives from distant symbols into a single instance or fragment a coherent symbol across multiple predictions. Motivated by the professional "retrieve-and-transform" CAD design workflow, we reformulate this task as a Template Fitting problem, where each foreground instance is detected by retrieving and aligning a canonical template from a library, enforcing structural completeness by construction. Building on this formulation, we present an autoregressive transformer that unifies template retrieval and pose prediction within a single end-to-end pipeline. The framework treats the template library as an explicit geometric memory, parsing background regions in parallel via learnable background tokens and synthesizing foreground instances autoregressively while attending to template-specific geometry at each step. Experiments on FloorplanCAD and our newly collected IndustryCAD dataset, a more challenging benchmark with complex industrial symbols, heavy occlusion, and wide scale variation, demonstrate state-of-the-art performance with particularly large gains on IndustryCAD. Project page: https://tempfit-project.github.io/.

candidates.title: Neural Centroidal Voronoi Tessellations
candidates.abstract: Centroidal Voronoi tessellation (CVT) is a fundamental primitive for high-quality surface sampling and isotropic remeshing in computer graphics. However, computing surface CVTs with classical solvers remains expensive: each optimization step repeatedly constructs restricted Voronoi diagrams (RVDs) and integrates quantities over their surface cells. We introduce Neural CVT , a learning-based surface-CVT solver that replaces these costly geometric computations with a recurrent neural optimizer, accelerating CVT optimization by one to two orders of magnitude in our benchmarks while preserving geometric fidelity. Given an input surface, we sample a dense point cloud and extract multi-scale geometric descriptors with a graph neural encoder. A lightweight recurrent optimizer then refines seed positions over a small number of iterations, aggregating interpolated surface features and optimization history to predict per-seed displacements. The framework is trained self-supervised using CVT objectives that promote uniform distributions and, when desired, feature alignment. Across diverse organic and CAD-like shapes, Neural CVT generalizes to unseen geometry, initialization strategies, and seed densities, producing isotropic, feature-preserving remeshes comparable to state-of-the-art offline optimization methods at a fraction of the computational cost. The code and trained models are available at https://github.com/sig-pku/NeuralCVT.

candidates.title: PneuGen: Task-Driven Agentic Co-Design of Soft Pneumatic Robots
candidates.abstract: Task-driven design of soft robots requires the consideration of factors such as geometry, morphology, material properties, and actuation, resulting in a large and complex design space that is challenging to explore. Computational optimisation methods leverage signals from simulation to iteratively improve designs to achieve task objectives. However, these methods typically demand high computational load for both optimisation and simulation. We present PneuGen, an agentic co-design framework for soft robots that leverages Large Language Model (LLM) agents to search over the soft robot design space efficiently. A designer agent proposes design programs from a parametric component library, and a separate critic agent analyses simulation diagnostics and recommends targeted revisions. Fitted module response models provide reusable physical priors relating geometry and pressure to deformation. Design programs are automatically validated and converted into finite-element simulations, enabling iterative evaluation. Across grasping tasks on primitive shapes and challenging objects, as well as shape-matching tasks that require multi-directional planar and 3D deformation, the proposed framework significantly outperforms prior computational optimisation baselines. Ablation experiments also highlight the utility of the critic agent and the module response model in facilitating efficient design. We additionally demonstrate the agent-generated soft robot designs in real-world shape-matching and grasping tasks.

candidates.title: GOPR-CAD: Graph-of-Operations Progressive Reasoning for CAD Generation
candidates.abstract: Generating accurate CAD models requires substantial engineering expertise and careful control of geometry, topology, and mechanical constraints. Text-to-CAD aims to simplify this process, but current LLM-based methods often generate CAD programs directly. Language models remain unreliable when producing long code while coordinating coupled geometric, topological, and dimensional constraints. Consequently, executable programs may still produce structurally incorrect models, which execution rate and rendered appearance may fail to reveal. To address these limitations, we propose GOPR-CAD, an agentic Text-to-CAD pipeline based on Graph-of-Operations Progressive Reasoning. A language model acts as a decision agent over encapsulated CAD operations and progressively constructs an executable operation graph, which a deterministic compiler converts into the final CAD model. This separation requires no additional training and supports different language models. To evaluate structural fidelity, we construct MHCAD, a benchmark of 300 standard mechanical part requirements derived from Machinery's Handbook. Their explicit structures enable reference-free STEP/B-rep evaluation. GOPR-CAD achieves 82.7% Structural Yield on MHCAD, and 87.2% Structural Yield on an external CADPrompt subset.

A language model acts as a decision agent over encapsulated CAD operations and progressively constructs an executable operation graph, which a deterministic compiler converts into the final CAD model. This separation requires no additional training and supports different language models. To evaluate structural fidelity, we construct MHCAD, a benchmark of 300 standard mechanical part requirements derived from Machinery's Handbook. Their explicit structures enable reference-free STEP/B-rep evaluation. GOPR-CAD achieves 82.7% Structural Yield on MHCAD, and 87.2% Structural Yield on an external CADPrompt subset.

candidates.title: FG-DSA: Frequency-Guided Depthwise Separable Attention for Efficient Dense Prediction
candidates.abstract: Dense prediction and generative modeling remain challenging in resource-constrained environments, particularly because repeated downsampling can lead to the loss of spatial details and less accurate object boundaries. Although attention mechanisms have been widely adopted to address semantic ambiguity, preserving high-frequency information while maintaining computational efficiency remains an important challenge. To address this issue, we propose Frequency-Guided Depthwise Separable Attention for Efficient Dense Prediction (FG-DSA), a framework that integrates frequency-domain information into lightweight vision architectures for dense visual understanding and generation. Specifically, FG-DSA uses a 2D Fast Fourier Transform (FFT)-based high-pass filtering module to guide spatial attention, aiming to retain fine-grained features and improve object-boundary representation. Experimental results show that FG-DSA can improve boundary-related performance in semantic segmentation under the evaluated setting. Beyond discriminative tasks, we also examine its application in a generative U-Net for single-step image restoration. The results suggest that incorporating FG-DSA can enhance reconstruction quality and help preserve high-frequency details.

candidates.title: RTLREX: LLM-Guided Framework for Exact High-Level RTL Recovery
candidates.abstract: Hardware designs may be available only as gate-level netlists or input-output descriptions when the original register-transfer-level (RTL) design and documentation are not accessible. Low-level representations obscure word-level computation and its finite-width behavior. Recovering high-level RTL from such representations therefore helps engineers understand a circuit's functionality and enables RTL rewriting and resynthesis. A plausible function model is also insufficient unless the generated RTL is equivalent to the original circuit for all input combinations. In this paper, we present RTLREX, a large language model (LLM)-guided framework that coordinates domain-specific tools for function recovery, RTL generation, independent verification, and cost-guided rewriting. Independent verification establishes equivalence between the recovered RTL and the original circuit. The LLM uses tool feedback to select further analyses, revise candidate RTL, and propose syntax-cost reductions. Experiments on 30 benchmarks from Problem A of the ICCAD 2022 CAD Contest show that RTLREX recovers equivalent high-level RTL for all benchmarks, surpassing the state-of-the-art method WolFEx in recovery coverage. On benchmarks recovered by both methods, RTLREX reduces mean syntax cost by 20.5% relative to WolFEx. On complete truth-table benchmarks from the IWLS 2026 Contest, our framework reduces mean syntax cost by 95.7% relative to an LLM agent baseline on the benchmarks validated by both methods.

candidates.title: Distinguishing Extraction Failures and Clinical Discordance with LLM Uncertainty on Radiology Reports
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to structure data from unstructured text, but extraction errors remain inevitable. We evaluated whether LLM uncertainty could distinguish extraction failure from true clinical discordance. In 5{,}225 vessels from 1{,}045 patients undergoing coronary CT angiography (CCTA) for suspected coronary artery disease (CAD), we evaluated token-level and self-reported LLM uncertainty during extraction of vessel-level stenosis severity. Extraction failure was defined as disagreement between LLM-extracted stenosis and expert annotations. Clinical discordance was defined as disagreement in obstructive CAD status between CCTA and subsequent invasive coronary angiography (ICA). Incremental discrimination was assessed after adjustment for stenosis severity, calcium burden, and coronary vessel. Extraction failure was evaluated in 1{,}077 vessels from 253 patients with expert annotations, and clinical discordance in 1{,}641 vessels from 729 patients undergoing ICA within 90 days. Token-level Stenosis Margin showed the strongest association with extraction failure (adjusted OR, 4.15 [95\% CI, 2.57--6.69]; $P<0.001$) and clinical discordance (adjusted OR, 1.22 [95\% CI, 1.04--1.43]; $P=0.118$). Stenosis Margin significantly improved discrimination of extraction failure ($Δ$AUC, +0.06 [95\% CI, +0.03 to +0.09]; $P=0.001$), but not clinical discordance ($Δ$AUC, +0.01 [95\% CI, $-0.00$ to +0.02]; $P=0.245$). In a nested cohort of 138 vessels from 57 patients, 38 of 42 clinically discordant vessels (90\%) were extracted correctly. LLM uncertainty improved identification of extraction failure but not clinical discordance, suggesting that uncertainty may identify errors introduced during data extraction but may not generalize to discordance in underlying clinical data.

candidates.title: PhyCAD: Physics-Aware Text-to-CAD Generation via Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
candidates.abstract: Language-driven computer-aided design (CAD) generation enables the creation of editable parametric models from text, yet geometric correctness alone does not ensure physical feasibility. We present PhyCAD, a framework for physics-aware Text-to-CAD generation that trains language models to produce executable CadQuery programs under geometric and physical constraints. To support this setting, we construct a Text-to-CAD dataset that links parametric CAD models with geometric specifications, loading conditions, and physical constraints. We further develop an automated CAD--CAE verifier that combines program execution, geometric checks, and finite element analysis to provide feedback for model training. A key learning challenge is to prioritize joint satisfaction of geometric and physical constraints while retaining informative feedback on partial progress. A flat aggregation of heterogeneous rewards can obscure this priority, allowing improvements in individual criteria to compensate for unmet design requirements. We therefore introduce a Hierarchical Balanced Advantage for Group Relative Policy Optimization, grouping candidates into levels according to their verification status and combining between-level progress with objective-wise peer ranking within each level. This formulation preserves cross-level priority in the training signal while providing fine-grained feedback for satisfying constraints and improving feasible designs. Experiments across multiple language models show that PhyCAD consistently improves joint geometric and physical constraint satisfaction. These results demonstrate the value of verifiable engineering feedback for advancing language-driven CAD generation beyond geometric reconstruction toward physics-aware design.

candidates.title: Done Is Not Correct: Measuring Silent Failures and Self-Verification Calibration When LLM Agents Take CAD Actions
candidates.abstract: When a large language model (LLM) agent writes parametric CAD code from a natural-language specification, syntactic success decouples from semantic correctness. We release a benchmark and harness that measure this gap directly: 13 specification tasks whose every requirement maps to machine-checkable properties of the produced B-rep, measured by the kernel against published tolerance bands, with reference solutions and the full graded attempt corpus. The exact, self-audited oracle isolates two quantities no prior CAD benchmark reports: the silent-failure rate (a valid, renderable solid, an explicit completion claim, and at least one failed semantic check) and completion-claim calibration. Across four models from four vendors (156 attempts per architecture), single-shot agents claimed completion on 98% of attempts and were silently wrong on 14.1%; a tool-use loop that enforces measure-then-claim cut silent failures to 3.2% and raised claim precision from 64% to 96%, and a four-model ablation attributes the change to the claim contract rather than the feedback. A planner-coder-checker pipeline matched that precision at lower coverage with no success gain. Stated confidence was miscalibrated single-shot (ECE 0.32) and became informative under verification for three of four models. Hardening our own oracle flipped 18 of 519 regraded verdicts from pass to fail and none in reverse; a blind expert audit overturned 3 of the 18 silent failures outside the one ambiguously specified task; and fourfold scaling of every tolerance band leaves the contrast intact.
